thread:
Jenna: Quick one — POC customer reporting responses getting suddenly truncated and sometimes a 413 from our API when they send a big context (10k+ messages compressed into one payload).
Carmen: Ugh. Any error body from Redwood API? 413 typically is gateway/body limit.
Jenna: They see `HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large` in their client. On successful but truncated calls we get 200 with half the output missing (stops mid-token).
Raj: Can you grab the original curl and the Content-Length? Also which model and max_tokens are they requesting?
Jenna: Here is the curl they used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @payload.json` Payload size ~7.3MB, model `rwd-3-large`, max_tokens 8192.
Lee: Two things: 1) 413 = our edge/gateway rejecting by body size (nginx/ingress). 2) truncation on 200 smells like streaming/chunk assembly issue on the client or our proxy cutting the response.
infra-bot: Deploy note — we bumped `client_max_body_size` on the public ingress to 8M last week for traffic shaping. Current limit = 8M.
Carmen: That explains 7.3MB hitting borderline. If their payload hits >8M sometimes (gzip variance) it will be rejected. For truncated responses, need proxy logs and request id.
Jenna: Asked customer for raw request id: `req_01G9XYZ...` — they sent it.
Raj: I pulled the request id — edge logs show `413` at 2025-08-14T16:12:03Z. Upstream runtime logs show the request reached runner but then connection from proxy timed out and closed the stream at token 416.
Lee: Timeout+proxy close = client sees truncated 200. Likely our streaming buffer hit limit or the proxy closed early.
Carmen: Quick mitigations to try with the customer: 1) gzip the payload (Content-Encoding: gzip) — reduces size significantly. 2) split context into multiple calls and stitch on client. 3) use the streaming API so the proxy chunking is handled better.
Jenna: Customer tried gzip, got accepted — no 413 — but still saw truncation sometimes when streaming.
Raj: For streaming truncation, ask them to use `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with keepalive and to surface connection-level errors. Also share curl example: ```curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -H "Content-Encoding: gzip"```
Lee: Long-term: for enterprise POCs we recommend Dedicated capacity — higher ingress limits and fewer proxy hops. Also we can recommend lowering max_tokens per call and use KV-cache/prefix caching to reduce context size.
Jenna: Customer asked whether Dedicated means extra cost for more tokens — yes, Dedicated is a capacity/reservation model; token costs still apply but you get predictable throughput and we can accommodate larger per-request payloads.
Carmen: Also note model token limits: `rwd-3-large` supports 64k context (logical tokens) but transport limits may still block. We should clearly document payload size vs token limits in the POC guide.
deploy-bot: FYI — submitted infra ticket INF-5423 to increase ingress limit to 16M for the next canary.
Raj: Action items: Carmen to send customer gzip + chunked examples; Lee to capture exact proxy error pattern and coordinate with infra; infra to confirm canary for 16M. Jenna to keep customer updated and offer Dedicated trial if they want to avoid further infra blockers.
Carmen: I'll also request that we add a short note to sales POC checklist: "If payload >5MB recommend gzip or Dedicated".
Jenna: Thanks team — keeping customer in the loop now.
Lee: If they want immediate workaround, show them how to compress conversation with summarization/embedding recall: reduce context by ~70% often.
Jenna: Got it, sending options now. :thumbsup:
